stt.error_native_desktop: Web Speech does not work in the desktop app. Use Whisper, Groq, Vosk, or the Chrome / Edge microphone page instead.
stt.migrated_to_whisper: Speech-to-text now uses Whisper on this PC (Web Speech does not work in the desktop app). Press Start once to download the {{model}} model{{size}}.
stt.azure_segmentation_silence_desc: Silence that ends a phrase. Lower gives faster final captions; too low splits sentences. 100-5000, default 500.
stt.vad_desc: Silero VAD decides when you speak. Only speech is transcribed; silence and background noise never are.
stt.vad_threshold_desc: How sure the detector must be that you are speaking. Lower catches quiet speech, higher ignores more noise. Default 0.5.
stt.vad_min_silence_desc: A pause this long closes the sentence and sends it. Shorter feels faster but can split sentences. Default 500.
stt.vad_max_utterance_desc: Longer speech is split at the quietest moment. Default 18000.
stt.whisper_desc: Runs locally with whisper.cpp. The first start downloads the selected model once; your voice never leaves this PC.
stt.whisper_model_desc: Bigger models are more accurate but slower on the CPU. Q5 / Q8 builds are smaller and faster with almost the same accuracy. English-only models are a little better for English.
stt.whisper_anime_hint: Anime-Whisper is a Japanese model for expressive speech. It is not downloaded: convert litagin/anime-whisper to a ggml .bin with whisper.cpp, then use it as a local model file below.
stt.whisper_language_desc: Setting your language is faster and more accurate than detection. English-only models always transcribe English.
stt.whisper_hallucination_filter_desc: Drops phantom phrases such as "Thanks for watching" when they make up a whole sentence, and collapses repeated loops.
stt.whisper_no_speech_threshold_desc: Drops a sentence when Whisper thinks it is not speech with more than this confidence. 1 turns it off. Default 0.6.
stt.whisper_hotwords_desc: Comma-separated names and terms Whisper should spell correctly.
stt.whisper_initial_prompt_desc: Optional text that sets the style and topic, for example "Casual chat in VRChat."
stt.whisper_threads_desc: Automatic uses about half your cores (at most 4) so games keep their CPU time.
stt.whisper_max_backlog_desc: Sentences that may wait for the model. If Whisper falls further behind, the oldest waiting sentence is skipped so captions stay current. Default 3.
stt.groq_desc: Whisper large-v3 Turbo on Groq's free plan: very accurate and fast. Needs an internet connection and a free API key; your speech is sent to Groq.
stt.openai_audio_prompt_desc: Names and terms to spell correctly, or a sentence that sets the style.
stt.vosk_desc: Runs locally. The model downloads once as a zip into app data, then loads offline.
stt.vosk_model_desc: Models are downloaded once and kept. Larger models are more accurate but slower.
stt.vosk_model_url_desc: Full URL of a Vosk model .zip. It replaces the catalog URL for the download; the file is still saved under app data as the selected model.
stt.shortcut_desc: Global shortcuts also work while Sigil is in the background, for example in VRChat.
stt.shortcut_hint_unsupported: That key cannot be used for a global shortcut.
stt.shortcut_hint_in_use: Another Sigil shortcut already uses this combination.
stt.shortcut_hint_needs_ctrl_alt: Add Ctrl, Alt or Win (Shift alone is not enough), or use an F-key, so the shortcut does not block normal typing.
stt.groq_limits_merge: Groq bills every request as at least 10 seconds. If you talk a lot, Sigil sends short sentences together (captions can then arrive a few seconds later), so the daily limit lasts a long stream.
stt.route_note_auto_language: The spoken language is detected for every sentence.
stt.route_note_language_id: A small language detector listens to each sentence before it is transcribed.
stt.route_note_generic_language_model: No model is made for this language, so a general multilingual model transcribes it.
stt.route_note_finals_only: Captions appear when you finish a sentence, without live partial captions.
stt.route_note_single_pass: Two-pass captions are off, so each sentence is transcribed once.
stt.route_note_few_cores_single_pass: This PC has too few processor cores to run two speech models at once, so each sentence is transcribed once.
stt.route_note_vc_running_single_pass: The voice changer is using the processor, so each sentence is transcribed once.
stt.route_note_gpu_unavailable: The graphics card cannot be used for speech recognition here, so it runs on the processor.
stt.route_note_gpu_runtime_unavailable: The GPU speech runtime is not installed, so speech recognition runs on the processor. Import it in Models & Runtimes to use the graphics card.
stt.route_note_gpu_denied_vc_running: The voice changer is using the graphics card, so captions run on the processor. Choose the GPU tier to share the card anyway.
stt.route_note_vc_shares_gpu: Captions and the voice changer share the graphics card.
stt.route_note_gpu_full: Too little video memory is free for a GPU model right now, so it runs on the processor.
stt.route_note_no_gpu_model_for_language: No GPU model is better than the processor model for this language.
stt.route_note_nemotron_needs_language: Live partial captions need to know the language: pick one to turn them on.
stt.route_note_never_route: A model was skipped because it does not handle this language well.
stt.route_note_no_engine: No speech model is available for this language.
stt.route_note_routing_table_invalid: The speech model table could not be read (see the log).
stt.local_desc: Sigil picks the best speech models for your language and your PC and runs them here. Models download once, only after you agree; your voice never leaves this PC.
stt.local_language_desc: Choosing the language you speak gives live captions and the most accurate model. Detection works sentence by sentence, with captions after each sentence.
stt.local_tier_desc: Best for my PC uses the graphics card when it has room and a better model for your language, and leaves it to the voice changer when the card is small.
stt.local_two_pass_desc: Shows live captions while you speak, then replaces each sentence with a more accurate transcription. Needs a larger download and more computing power; Sigil uses one pass when this PC cannot afford two.
stt.local_smart_turn: Detect when you finish speaking (Smart Turn)
stt.local_smart_turn_desc: Lets translation, text-to-speech and the VRChat chatbox send sooner when you have finished your turn. Captions are not affected. Adds a 9 MB download.
stt.local_hotwords_desc: Comma-separated names and terms to recognize reliably, such as your friends' names. Used by the models that support it.
stt.local_route_error: Could not check the speech models: {{error}}
stt.local_route_desktop_only: Speech recognition on this PC needs the desktop app.
stt.local_route_summary_two_pass: Live captions while you speak, then a more accurate final text for each sentence.
stt.local_route_none: No speech model is available for this language on this PC.
stt.local_role_fallback: Backup if the graphics card fails
stt.local_consent_smaller_hint: Or choose the smaller setup ({{size}}): live captions with one pass, slightly less accurate.
stt.local_consent_smaller_hint_free: Or skip the second, more accurate pass: it needs no download, and captions stay live.
stt.local_consent_smaller_hint_finals: Or choose the smaller setup ({{size}}): one model, with captions after each sentence instead of live captions.
stt.local_consent_smaller_hint_finals_free: Or skip live captions: that needs no download, and captions appear after each sentence.

stt.browser_keep_open: The page runs speech recognition in {{browser}} and sends the text to Sigil. Keep it open while speech-to-text runs.

stt.local_onboarding_desc: Recommended. Sigil picks the best speech models for your language and your PC; they download once, after you agree.
stt.local_status_language_auto: The live model is guessing the spoken language. Choose your language for more accurate live captions.
stt.local_status_hotwords_unavailable: This model cannot use hotwords; recognition continues without them.
stt.route_note_vc_unknown_single_pass: The voice changer is starting and may use the processor, so each sentence is transcribed once. Restart captions after it has started to get two-pass captions.
stt.route_note_no_cpu_fallback: If the graphics card fails, captions keep the live text instead of transcribing again on the processor, which has too few cores or is running the voice changer.
stt.groq_limits_paced: The free plan allows 20 requests per minute, 2,000 per day and 2 hours of audio per hour. Sigil sends one request per sentence and paces them to stay inside these limits. Sentences that have to wait are sent together; speech that would wait more than 2 minutes is skipped, and the status line says so.
stt.gemini_desc: Google's live transcription on your own Gemini API key: very accurate captions in 85+ languages, sent as you speak. Sessions are renewed in the background every few minutes without losing words.
stt.gemini_privacy: Your microphone audio is sent to Google while this runs. On the free tier, Google may use it to improve its products.
stt.gemini_key_placeholder_shared: Empty: uses the key from the Translation settings
stt.gemini_key_shared: Using the Gemini key from the Translation settings. Enter a key here to use a different one.
stt.gemini_key_missing: Enter a Gemini API key here or in the Translation settings (Gemini provider).
stt.gemini_get_key: Get a free key at Google AI Studio
stt.gemini_mode_transcribe_desc: Publishes your speech as captions. The Translation service can translate them as usual.
stt.gemini_mode_translate_desc: One Gemini session publishes your captions and their translation, a few seconds behind your speech. Gemini detects the language you speak.
stt.gemini_language_desc: Choosing your language makes recognition more accurate. Detection handles 85+ languages.
stt.gemini_formatting_desc: Smart removes "um" and "uh" and formats numbers and punctuation.
stt.gemini_vocabulary_placeholder: Names, game terms, ... separated by commas
stt.gemini_vocabulary_desc: Names and terms Gemini should recognize, separated by commas (up to 1,000; about 100 works best).
stt.gemini_echo: Repeat speech already in the target language
stt.gemini_echo_desc: When you speak the target language, the translation repeats it, so every line gets a translation caption.
stt.gemini_model_desc: Google renames preview models from time to time. Change the id here if Gemini says the model is not found.
stt.gemini_rotate_desc: Gemini ends a session after 10 minutes, so Sigil opens the next one in advance and switches at a pause, with both listening for a moment so no words are lost. Now: every {{minutes}} min.
stt.gemini_api_version_desc: Leave on v1beta unless Google moves the Live API to another version. If Google's session token service has moved, Sigil tries the other version by itself.
stt.gemini_error_no_key: Gemini Live needs an API key. Enter one in the Speech-to-text settings or set the Gemini key in the Translation settings.
stt.gemini_error_model: Enter the Gemini model id in the Gemini Live settings (Advanced).
stt.gemini_error_target: Choose the language Gemini Live should translate into.
stt.gemini_error_desktop_only: Gemini Live needs the desktop app (it uses Sigil's microphone capture).
stt.gemini_error_key: Gemini refused the API key ({{detail}}). Check the key in the Speech-to-text or Translation settings.
stt.gemini_error_rejected: Gemini refused the session: {{detail}}. Check the model id, the language and the API version in the Gemini Live settings.
stt.gemini_error_quota: Gemini's usage limits were reached ({{detail}}). Try again later or use another speech recognizer.
stt.gemini_error_lost: Lost the connection to Gemini and could not reconnect ({{detail}}).
stt.gemini_error_connect: Could not connect to Gemini ({{detail}}). Check your internet connection. If it keeps failing, try the other API version under Advanced in the Gemini Live settings.
stt.gemini_status_reconnecting: The connection to Gemini was lost ({{detail}}). Reconnecting (attempt {{attempt}})… What you say meanwhile is sent once it is back.
stt.gemini_status_wait: Gemini asked to wait ({{detail}}). Trying again in {{seconds}} s…
stt.gemini_status_gap: Gemini was unreachable for a while, so some speech could not be transcribed.
stt.gemini_status_translation_running: The Translation service is running too, so your lines are translated twice. Stop it while Live Translate runs.
stt.gemini_status_options_dropped: Gemini did not accept the custom vocabulary or the transcript style ({{detail}}), so it runs without them.
stt.gemini_detail_setup_timeout: Gemini did not answer the session setup
stt.gemini_detail_handshake: the live connection could not be opened, code {{code}}
stt.gemini_detail_token_timeout: the session token request timed out
stt.gemini_detail_no_token: Gemini's reply contained no session token
stt.backend_not_ready: This speech recognizer is not available in this build yet.
stt.local_music_gate_desc: Skips stretches that sound like music or singing, such as world music in VRChat, instead of turning them into captions. Needs a small extra download.
stt.local_interim_desc: Shows words while you are still speaking. Turn it off to get each sentence only once it is finished: Sigil then does not run the live model whenever a more accurate one also runs, which saves processor time. A language that only has a live model keeps using it, and its finished sentences still appear. Applies the next time speech-to-text starts.
stt.lang_offer_system: Your Windows language is {{language}}. Lock captions to {{language}}?
stt.lang_offer_why: Setting the language usually makes captions more accurate (most of all for European languages) and uses less memory. Locking restarts running captions at once when the {{language}} models are already installed; otherwise it applies the next time you press Start.
stt.lang_offer_result_restarted: Locked to {{language}}. Captions restarted with the {{language}} models.
stt.lang_offer_result_next_start: Locked to {{language}}. It applies the next time you press Start.
stt.lang_offer_result_download: Locked to {{language}}. The next Start downloads the {{language}} speech models first, and asks before it does. You can review them in Speech to Text. Until then, captions that start by themselves keep detecting the language automatically.
stt.lang_offer_log_restarted: Captions locked to {{language}}; they restarted with the {{language}} models.
stt.lang_offer_log_next_start: Captions locked to {{language}}; it applies the next time Start is pressed.
stt.lang_offer_log_download: Captions locked to {{language}}; the next Start downloads the {{language}} models first. Until then, captions that start by themselves keep detecting the language.
stt.onboarding_language_hint: Setting your language is the biggest step for accurate captions.
stt.local_consent_auto_hint: Tip: you are on Detect automatically, which needs a language-detection model on top of a general one. If you cancel and choose your language in Speech to Text first, Sigil usually downloads less and the captions are more accurate.
stt.local_log_auto_fallback: The {{language}} speech models are not downloaded, so captions started with automatic language detection. Open Speech-to-text and press Start to download the {{language}} models.
stt.tab_rewrite_desc: Rewrite each sentence with a language model. Runs next to speech to text.
stt.moonshine_retired: Moonshine server mode was retired. Speech to Text now uses "Built-in (on your PC)": nothing to install, and your microphone and language carried over. The first Start asks before downloading models.
stt.local_offer_message_chrome: You're using Chrome's speech recognition, which sends your voice to Google. Sigil now has its own speech recognition that runs on your PC. In our English test it made about {{ours}} mistakes per 100 words, versus about {{theirs}} for Chrome. It also works without internet and keeps your voice on your PC. Sigil starts with your system's default microphone and detects your language automatically; you can change both in Speech to Text. The first time you press Start, Sigil asks before downloading the speech models (about {{size}}).
stt.local_offer_message_edge: You're using Edge's speech recognition, which sends your voice to Microsoft. Sigil now has its own speech recognition that runs on your PC. In our English test it made about {{ours}} mistakes per 100 words, versus about {{theirs}} for Edge. It also works without internet and keeps your voice on your PC. Sigil starts with your system's default microphone and detects your language automatically; you can change both in Speech to Text. The first time you press Start, Sigil asks before downloading the speech models (about {{size}}).
stt.local_offer_message_other: Switch to Sigil's built-in speech recognition, which runs on your PC? Your microphone and language stay the same. The first time you press Start, Sigil asks before downloading the speech models (about {{size}}).
stt.local_status_retrying: Speech recognition is not running ({{detail}}). Trying again in {{seconds}} s…
stt.local_status_start_retry: Speech recognition could not start ({{detail}}). Trying again in {{seconds}} s…
stt.local_status_start_retry_capture: Speech recognition could not open the microphone ({{detail}}). Another app may be using it. Trying again in {{seconds}} s…
stt.status_reconnecting_slow: {{detail}} Still trying: the next attempt is in {{seconds}} s…
stt.error_azure_closed: The connection to Azure Speech ended.
stt.status_reconnecting_limited: {{detail}} The service is limiting requests, so the next attempt is in {{seconds}} s…

tts.neural_sidecar_desc: You run a program that answers GET /health and POST /speech with JSON { text, voice }. Example: scripts/neural-sidecar/tts_sidecar.py (port 8766). See that folder’s README.
tts.ep_cuda_plain: NVIDIA GPU / CUDA (needs NVIDIA drivers and CUDA runtime)
tts.neural_onnx_browse_unavailable: Folder browse is available in the desktop app.
tts.http_list_fetch_failed: Could not load voices from the server. Check the URL and that the service is running.
tts.kokoro_desc: Kokoro FastAPI–compatible server (OpenAI-style /v1/audio/speech). Example: docker run -p 8880:8880 ghcr.io/remsky/kokoro-fastapi-cpu
tts.melo_desc: MeloTTS HTTP API. Example: docker run -p 8888:8888 myshell-ai/melotts
tts.chatterbox_desc: Chatterbox TTS HTTP server (see your stack’s compose or docs). Default URL is often port 5555.
tts.fish_desc: Fish Speech API. Example: docker run -p 8080:8080 fishaudio/fish-speech
tts.uberduck_voice_desc_key: Voices load once a valid API key is entered.
tts.native_unavailable: Speech synthesis is not available in this webview.
tts.native_voice_missing: The selected voice is not installed on this PC. Choose another voice.
tts.fish_hosted_hint: Fish Audio's hosted API: set the server URL to https://api.fish.audio, enter your API key, and pick a model such as s2.1-pro-free. A self-hosted server needs a key only if it was started with --api-key.
tts.voicevox_desc: Japanese character voices from a VOICEVOX-compatible engine (VOICEVOX or AivisSpeech) running on this PC. Download:
tts.voicevox_aivis_hint: AivisSpeech voices sound best at pitch 0. Intonation sets how strongly the style's emotion comes through.
tts.voicevox_no_speakers: No speakers found. Is the engine running?
tts.voicevox_host_error_empty: Enter the engine URL, for example http://localhost:50021.
tts.voicevox_host_error_invalid_url: "{{host}}" is not a valid engine URL. Use a URL such as http://localhost:50021.
tts.voicevox_host_error_remote_http: Sigil can reach {{host}} only over https. Plain http works only for engines on this PC (localhost or 127.0.0.1).
tts.voicevox_not_running: No VOICEVOX-compatible engine answered at {{host}}. Start VOICEVOX or AivisSpeech (or check the URL), then try again.
tts.voicevox_timeout: The engine at {{host}} did not answer in time.
tts.voicevox_not_responding: The engine at {{host}} answered with HTTP {{status}}.
tts.azure_connect_failed: Could not connect with this key and region ("{{region}}"). Check both, and your internet connection. Details: {{error}}
tts.azure_connect_timeout: The speech service for region "{{region}}" did not answer in time. Check the region and your internet connection.
tts.route_vc_hint: Speech is mixed into your microphone before conversion, so it comes out in your converted voice. What happens to your microphone meanwhile is set in the voice changer (Microphone while TTS plays).
tts.route_vc_not_running: The voice changer is not running: speech plays on the output device until you start it.
tts.route_self_playing: This voice plays by itself on its own output, so it is spoken as a whole and cannot go through the voice changer.
tts.local_neural_desc: Natural voices that run on this PC's processor: Kokoro (English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese), Kitten (English) and Piper voices for many more languages. No server to run; each voice downloads once.
tts.local_neural_desktop_only: Local voices work in the desktop app.
tts.local_neural_list_failed: The list of local voices could not be read.
tts.local_neural_folder_hint: An official sherpa-onnx Kokoro, Kitten or Piper voice folder, or a Sigil speech package (config.json with its model and voices).
tts.local_neural_not_downloaded: {{title}} is not downloaded yet. Download it in the voice panel or in Models & Runtimes.
tts.neural_onnx_desc_local_engine: Runs Kitten voices on this PC's processor, from a Hugging Face repo or a speech package folder. Speech plays through the selected output device and can go into the voice changer (Routing below).
tts.neural_onnx_prefer_local_neural: More voices and languages (Kokoro, Piper) are in the local voice backend.
tts.neural_onnx_hub_invalid: "{{repo}}" is not a valid Hugging Face repo id (org/name).
tts.neural_onnx_hub_catalog_reason: This Kitten model downloads as Sigil's verified package (a copy downloaded by an earlier Sigil version also keeps working):
tts.neural_onnx_hub_download_note: The model downloads from Hugging Face the first time the voice starts.
tts.neural_onnx_local_hint_v2: A speech package folder (config.json plus the model and voice files it names), or an official sherpa-onnx Kokoro, Kitten or Piper voice folder.
tts.local_neural_ja_note: Japanese: kana are read well, but kanji may get Chinese readings. For natural Japanese, VOICEVOX or AivisSpeech sound better.
tts.openai_speech_desc: Any server that speaks the OpenAI text-to-speech API (/v1/audio/speech): Kokoro-FastAPI, Chatterbox, Voxtral, IndexTTS or VoxCPM2 on vLLM, Qwen3-TTS (qwentts.cpp), and others. Audio streams as it is generated, so speech starts before the sentence is finished.
tts.openai_speech_voices_loaded: {{n}} voices on this server. Type to filter.
tts.openai_speech_no_voices: This server does not list its voices. Type the voice id.
tts.openai_speech_test_text: Hello! This is how my voice sounds.
tts.openai_speech_extra_hint: Server-specific options merged into every request, for example {"lang_code": "j"} for Kokoro-FastAPI or {"exaggeration": 0.7} for Chatterbox.
tts.openai_speech_extra_invalid: Extra request fields must be a JSON object, for example {"lang_code": "a"}.
tts.openai_speech_url_missing: Enter the server URL, for example http://127.0.0.1:8880/v1.
tts.openai_speech_unreachable: No speech server answered at {{url}}. Start it (or check the URL), then try again.
tts.http_legacy_openai_hint: Speech streams through the OpenAI-compatible client. For Voxtral, IndexTTS, VoxCPM2 or Qwen3-TTS servers, choose "OpenAI-compatible (HTTP)".
tts.local_offer_message: Sigil can now speak with Kokoro, a natural voice that runs on this PC (English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian and Portuguese, plus Piper voices for many more languages). Switch text-to-speech to "Kokoro / Piper (local)"? The voice (about 360 MB) downloads only after you agree in its panel.
tts.local_offer_switched: Text-to-speech now uses "Kokoro / Piper (local)". Download the voice in its panel to start speaking.
tts.openai_speech_timeout_hint: How long the server may take before the first audio of a sentence (up to 600 s; automatic gives servers on this PC or the LAN more time for long sentences). Once audio plays, a pause longer than 110 s ends the sentence.
tts.qwen3_desc: Expressive voices on your graphics card: 9 built-in voices that follow style instructions, any voice from your voice library cloned from a short clip, or a new voice described in words. Speaks Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian, and starts playing while the rest of the sentence is still being made.
tts.qwen3_desktop_only: Qwen3-TTS runs in the Sigil desktop app.
tts.qwen3_last_sentence: Last sentence: first sound after {{first}} ms, {{seconds}} s of speech.
tts.qwen3_mode_clone: Clone a voice from your library
tts.qwen3_design_large_only: Describing a voice always uses the 1.7B model.
tts.qwen3_reason_vc_running: {{size}}: the voice changer is using the graphics card, so the smaller model keeps your voice smooth.
tts.qwen3_reason_shared_gpu: {{size}}: other models Sigil has loaded leave too little video memory for the larger one.
tts.qwen3_reason_small_gpu: {{size}}: the larger model does not fit on this graphics card.
tts.qwen3_reason_cpu: No suitable graphics card was found, so it runs on the processor.
tts.qwen3_swap_blocked: The {{size}} model is recommended right now but is not downloaded, so the loaded model keeps speaking. Download it below to switch automatically.
tts.qwen3_cpu_slow: On the processor most PCs make speech slower than it plays, so sentences may pause. Kokoro is the better voice without a graphics card.
tts.qwen3_pack_hint: The Qwen3-TTS server is not downloadable yet: use Import with the server zip you were given (built with scripts/runtime-packs/qwentts).
tts.qwen3_speaker_ryan: dynamic male voice with strong rhythm
tts.qwen3_speaker_vivian: bright, slightly edgy young female voice
tts.qwen3_speaker_uncle_fu: seasoned male voice, low and mellow
tts.qwen3_speaker_eric: lively Chengdu male voice, Sichuan accent
tts.qwen3_instruction_placeholder: For example: Speak in a happy, cheerful tone.
tts.qwen3_instruction_needs_large: Style instructions need the 1.7B model; the 0.6B model speaks without them.
tts.qwen3_clone_hint: A clean 3 to 10 second clip of one person talking clones best, together with its transcript. Clips with music, echo or other voices clone poorly.
tts.qwen3_clone_voice_missing: Choose a voice from your voice library to clone.
tts.qwen3_design_hint: Describe age, gender, pitch, mood and speaking style. Keep the same seed to keep the voice steady from sentence to sentence.
tts.qwen3_design_description_missing: Describe the voice you want first.
tts.qwen3_preview_default: Hello! This is how I sound with Qwen3-TTS.
tts.qwen3_preview_needs_download: Download the model and the server first.
tts.qwen3_helper_failed: The Qwen3-TTS server stopped: {{error}}. The next sentence starts it again.
tts.qwen3_swap_failed: Qwen3-TTS could not switch model size: {{error}}
tts.ggml_desc: Four newer open voice models that run on your graphics card as small helper programs on this PC: NVIDIA Magpie, Breeze TTS 2, OmniVoice and Fish S2 Pro. They are early ports, so expect rough edges; Kokoro and Qwen3-TTS are the steadier choices.
tts.ggml_desktop_only: These voices run in the Sigil desktop app.
tts.ggml_engine_magpie_desc: Five clear voices (John, Sofia, Aria, Jason and Leo) that keep the same identity in English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Vietnamese and Hindi; the v2607 model adds Korean, Arabic and Brazilian Portuguese. Light: about 1.5 GB of video memory.
tts.ggml_engine_breeze_desc: Very natural English and Mandarin speech. Describe the voice you want in words, or clone one from your voice library and direct how it speaks. Needs about 4 GB of video memory, so it suits 12 GB cards that are not also running a GPU voice changer.
tts.ggml_engine_omnivoice_desc: Speaks more than 600 languages, in an automatic voice or one cloned from your voice library. A good pick for languages other voices lack. About 2.2 GB of video memory.
tts.ggml_engine_s2_desc: Fish Audio's expressive multilingual model with inline tags such as [laugh] or [whisper], in an automatic voice or one cloned from your voice library. Heavy: about 7 GB of video memory, best on 12 GB cards or more. It also works through the Fish Speech backend with Fish Audio's own server.
tts.ggml_last_sentence: Last sentence: first sound after {{first}} ms, {{seconds}} s of speech.
tts.ggml_model_magpie_v2607: Magpie v2607 (10 languages, converted on this PC)
tts.ggml_model_breeze_q8_0: Q8_0 (recommended, about 4 GB of video memory)
tts.ggml_model_breeze_q4_k: Q4_K (smaller, about 3 GB of video memory)
tts.ggml_model_omnivoice_f16: F16 (full precision, a little more video memory)
tts.ggml_model_s2_q6_k: Q6_K (better, about 8.5 GB of video memory)
tts.ggml_model_s2_q8_0: Q8_0 (best, about 10 GB of video memory)
tts.ggml_variant_missing: {{engine}} has no build for this choice; choose Automatic.
tts.ggml_variant_needs_cuda: The CUDA build needs an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 16 / RTX 20 or newer with driver 580 or newer. Choose Vulkan or Automatic.
tts.ggml_variant_needs_gpu: No suitable graphics card was found; choose the processor.
tts.ggml_cpu_slow: On the processor most PCs make speech much slower than it plays, so sentences will pause. Kokoro is the better voice without a graphics card.
tts.ggml_magpie_tokenizer_hint: The Magpie tokenizer is not downloadable on its own: run scripts/runtime-packs/nemo-speech/fetch-magpie-tokenizer.ps1 once (it fetches the 32 MB start of NVIDIA's model archive and checks every file), then choose Import and pick the folder it prints.
tts.ggml_magpie_v2607_hint: NVIDIA publishes Magpie v2607 only in its training format: convert it once with scripts/runtime-packs/nemo-speech/convert-magpie-v2607.ps1 (needs Python), then Import the model file and the tokenizer zip it writes.
tts.ggml_s2_pack_hint: The Fish S2 Pro server is not downloadable: build it with scripts/runtime-packs/s2/build.ps1 (or use a zip you were given), then choose Import.
tts.ggml_breeze_direction_placeholder: For example: Speak softly, a little sleepy.
tts.ggml_breeze_hint: Describe age, gender, pitch, mood and pace. Keep the same seed to keep a described voice steady from sentence to sentence. For sounds such as (laugh) or (sigh) in the text, raise the guidance to 2 or 3.
tts.ggml_clone_hint: A clean 3 to 10 second clip of one person talking clones best, together with its transcript. Clips with music, echo or other voices clone poorly.
tts.ggml_no_clone_breeze: Without a voice to clone, Breeze makes the voice you describe above.
tts.ggml_no_clone_omnivoice: Without a voice to clone, OmniVoice picks a voice; the seed keeps it the same from sentence to sentence.
tts.ggml_no_clone_s2: Without a voice to clone, Fish S2 Pro picks a new voice for every sentence: choose a voice from your library for a steady one.
tts.ggml_omnivoice_consent: I have the consent of the person whose voice this is
tts.ggml_omnivoice_disclose: I tell my audience this voice is AI
tts.ggml_omnivoice_disclose_on: The engine will not speak its AI notice before each cloned sentence.
tts.ggml_omnivoice_disclose_off: The engine speaks a short AI notice before each cloned sentence unless you tell your audience yourself.
tts.ggml_omnivoice_consent_missing: Confirm that you have the speaker's consent before cloning their voice with OmniVoice.
tts.ggml_magpie_languages_hint: For Korean, Arabic and Brazilian Portuguese choose the v2607 model. Mandarin and Japanese need a custom build of the server.
tts.ggml_magpie_language_unsupported: Magpie cannot speak this language ({{language}}); choose a language it speaks, or another voice engine.
tts.ggml_seed_placeholder: Empty: the same voice every sentence
tts.ggml_s2_hint: Write tags such as [laugh], [whisper] or [excited] into the text to direct the voice. The first sentence after loading takes longest.
tts.ggml_preview_default_magpie: Hello! This is a Magpie voice speaking through Sigil.
tts.ggml_preview_default_breeze: Hello! This is Breeze TTS 2 speaking through Sigil.
tts.ggml_preview_default_omnivoice: Hello! This is OmniVoice speaking through Sigil.
tts.ggml_preview_default_s2: Hello! This is Fish S2 Pro speaking through Sigil.
tts.ggml_unload: Unload the voice engine (frees video memory)
tts.sbv2_desc: Expressive Japanese character voices that run inside Sigil, with no server to start: AivisSpeech voices (.aivmx files, for example from AivisHub) and Style-Bert-VITS2 JP-Extra ONNX exports. They read Japanese text.
tts.sbv2_not_downloaded: {{title}} is not downloaded yet. Download it in the voice panel or in Models & Runtimes.
tts.sbv2_no_voice: Choose a Style-Bert-VITS2 voice first: add an .aivmx file in the voice panel.
tts.sbv2_list_failed: The voice list could not be read: {{error}}
tts.sbv2_no_voices: No voices yet. Drop an .aivmx file below, or the folder of a Style-Bert-VITS2 ONNX export.
tts.sbv2_drop_hint: Drop an .aivmx voice here (or the folder of a Style-Bert-VITS2 ONNX export)
tts.sbv2_import_one_at_a_time: One voice at a time: adding the first file.
tts.sbv2_style_weight_hint: How strongly the style's emotion comes through. 1 is how the voice was trained; much higher can sound strained.
tts.sbv2_style_weight_neutral: The neutral style is the voice's average, so the strength has no effect.
tts.sbv2_noise_hint: How much the delivery varies between sentences (Style-Bert-VITS2's noise settings; 0.6 and 0.8 by default).
tts.gpt_sovits_desc: Voices you trained with GPT-SoVITS (v2, v2Pro, v3 or v4), spoken by its api_v2 server on this PC or your network. The audio streams in as it is generated.
tts.gpt_sovits_unreachable: No GPT-SoVITS server answered at {{url}}. Start api_v2.py (or check the URL), then try again.
tts.gpt_sovits_gpt_weights: GPT weights (.ckpt, path on the server)
tts.gpt_sovits_sovits_weights: SoVITS weights (.pth, path on the server)
tts.gpt_sovits_weights_hint: Leave empty to keep the server's current model. Applied when speech starts.
tts.gpt_sovits_weights_applied: The server switched to these weights.
tts.gpt_sovits_weights_failed: Could not switch the GPT-SoVITS weights: {{error}}
tts.gpt_sovits_library_needs_local: Voice-library voices work with a server on this PC. For a server on another machine, enter the clip's path on that machine.
tts.gpt_sovits_reference_hint: A clean 3-10 s clip of the trained voice with its exact transcript gives the most natural result.
tts.gpt_sovits_no_reference: Choose a reference voice from the voice library, or enter the path of a reference clip on the GPT-SoVITS server.
tts.gpt_sovits_streaming_fragments: By sentence part (best quality, any version)
tts.gpt_sovits_extra_hint: api_v2 options merged into every request, for example {"top_k": 15, "temperature": 1, "text_split_method": "cut5"}.
tts.cloud_desktop_only: Online voices run in the Sigil desktop app.
tts.cloud_preview_failed: The test sentence could not be spoken: {{error}}
tts.cloud_fallback_desc: Online voices sometimes fail, hit their free limits or stop answering. With the local voice on, Kokoro speaks on this PC instead, starting with the sentence that failed, and keeps speaking until the service works again.
tts.cloud_fallback_enable: Use the local voice (Kokoro) when the service fails
tts.cloud_fallback_after_hint: If no sound has arrived after this long, Kokoro takes over. Errors such as a full quota switch at once, and a service that cannot be reached at all switches sooner.
tts.cloud_fallback_active: {{service}}: {{reason}}. The local voice speaks until the service works again.
tts.cloud_local_missing: {{service}}: the local voice (Kokoro) is not downloaded, so nothing can speak while the service fails. Download it in the voice's settings.
tts.cloud_local_load_failed: The local fallback voice could not be loaded: {{error}}
tts.cloud_reason_rate_limited: the free limit is used up for now
tts.cloud_reason_unavailable: the service is busy or unavailable
tts.cloud_reason_auth: the key or sign-in was refused
tts.cloud_reason_rejected: the request was refused (check the voice or model)
tts.edge_desc: Hundreds of natural voices in more than 70 languages, free and without a key: the voices of Microsoft Edge's Read aloud, streamed from Microsoft's servers. The service is unofficial and can change or fail, so keep the local voice on as a fallback.
tts.edge_voices_failed: The voice list could not be loaded: {{error}}
tts.edge_voice_invalid: "{{voice}}" is not an Edge voice name. Use one like en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural.
tts.gemini_desc: Google's most natural voices on your own Gemini API key: 30 voices that follow a style instruction, in more than 100 languages, streamed as they are made. The free tier has daily limits; when they run out, the local voice takes over.
tts.gemini_get_key: Get a free key at Google AI Studio
tts.gemini_check_ok: The key and the model work.
tts.gemini_key_hint: Gemini TTS needs a Gemini API key. A free one takes a minute to create at Google AI Studio.
tts.gemini_unreachable: Google could not be reached to check the Gemini key. Sentences use the local voice until it answers.
tts.gemini_model_flash_lite: Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS (faster, higher free limits)
tts.gemini_model_hint: Google renames preview models from time to time: if a model stops working, pick another one or type its id.
tts.gemini_voice_id_hint: Any voice Gemini knows: a name from Google's extended voice library, or the id of a voice you designed (voice_…). Unknown names are refused by Google, and the local voice takes over.
tts.gemini_style_hint: Describe how to speak, in any language. The style is never read aloud.
tts.gemini_preview_default: Hello! This is how I sound.
tts.gemini_base_url_hint: Leave empty for Google's API. Only change it to use a proxy in front of the Gemini API; the key is sent to that address.
tts.cloning_not_downloaded: {{title}} is not downloaded yet. Download it in these settings or in Models & Runtimes first.
tts.cloning_desktop_only: Runs inside the Sigil desktop app.
tts.cloning_preview_needs_download: Download the model and choose a voice first.
tts.pocket_desc: Kyutai's small voice-cloning model, on the processor: it speaks English in the voice of a clip from your voice library and needs about two cores, no graphics card.
tts.pocket_builtin_voice: No voice chosen: Pocket speaks with its built-in voice.
tts.pocket_english_only: Pocket TTS speaks English. For other languages use Chatterbox Multilingual, Qwen3-TTS or the local Kokoro voices.
tts.chatterbox_local_desc: Resemble AI's voice-cloning model, run by Sigil itself: it speaks 23 languages in the voice of a clip from your voice library. Best on a graphics card; it also works on the processor, more slowly.
tts.chatterbox_local_device_auto: Automatic (graphics card when there is one)
tts.chatterbox_local_cpu_note: On the processor each sentence takes a while to make, so speech starts later than on a graphics card.
tts.chatterbox_local_voice_required: Choose a voice from your voice library for Chatterbox Multilingual: it speaks in the voice it clones.

transl.pair_unknown_language: "{{code}}" is not a language code Sigil knows. Choose a language from the list.
transl.live_desc: These settings work while translation runs; no restart needed.
transl.glossary_desc: Terms the translation must use, such as names and game words. Only the terms that occur in a line are sent with it. Language models use the glossary; DeepL, Firefox Translations and NLLB ignore it.
transl.glossary_case_sensitive: Match upper and lower case exactly
transl.glossary_incomplete: Needs both the term and its translation; it is not sent until then.
transl.glossary_paste_placeholder:

transl.glossary_probe: Try a line to see which terms are sent
transl.glossary_probe_none: No glossary term occurs in this line.
transl.context_turns_hint: Language models and DeepL keep names and style consistent with the lines before. More lines make each request a little slower.
transl.context_background_placeholder: Example: A VRChat stream about horror games. Mewnah is the streamer; keep a casual tone.
transl.context_background_hint: Topic, names and speaking style, sent with every line to language models that support it.
transl.partials_local_agreement_hint: Shows only the words two partial translations in a row agree on, so captions grow without flickering. The full translation follows when you finish the sentence.
transl.partials_show_tentative_hint: Captions also show the newest words before they are confirmed; they may still change.
transl.partials_throttle_hint: Fewer partial requests save CPU, video memory and cloud quota; the newest partial always wins.
transl.partials_turn_end_hint: When Smart Turn says a sentence is not finished, it is joined with the next one and translated as one line.
transl.partials_field_turn_hold: Longest wait for the end of a turn (s)
transl.input_field_hint: Also translates what you type in the text field.
transl.status_missing_restart: Start translation again once they are installed.
transl.route_desc: For every line, Sigil tries the engines in order and moves on to the next one when an engine is not set up, cannot translate the pair, fails or takes too long. Set up each engine by choosing it as the provider once.
transl.route_chain_hint: The first engine that can translate the line wins.
transl.route_rules_hint: Use another engine order for some language pairs, for example a Japanese specialist for Japanese to English. The first matching rule wins.
transl.route_interim_hint: Partial captions change several times per sentence, so a fast engine keeps them up to date; the full translation still uses the order above.
transl.route_timeout_hint: After this long without an answer, the next engine is tried.
transl.route_cloud_fallback_hint: When an online engine fails, also try Firefox Translations and NLLB if they are not in the order.
transl.llm_desc: Translates with a language model: one Sigil runs on this PC, a free or paid cloud model, or a server you run yourself.
transl.llm_custom_hint: Any OpenAI-compatible server. Servers on another PC in your network are reached through Sigil.
transl.llm_gemini_hint: Create a free API key in Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com). Flash-Lite models answer fastest.
transl.llm_openrouter_hint: Model names look like google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite. Models ending in :free cost nothing but are rate limited.
transl.llm_check_ok: Connected: {{n}} models available, including this one.
transl.llm_check_ok_pick: Connected: {{n}} models available. Pick one below.
transl.llm_check_ok_empty: Connected. The server did not list its models.
transl.llm_check_model_missing: Connected, but "{{model}}" is not one of the {{n}} models. Pick one below or check the name.
transl.llm_format_uses_none: This format sends only the line itself (no earlier lines, glossary or background).
transl.llm_custom_prompt_hint: Placeholders: {source_lang}, {target_lang}, {text}, {context}, {glossary}, {background}. The line is always sent marked as text to translate, never as instructions.
transl.llm_custom_prompt_empty: The template is empty, so the general instruction prompt is used.
transl.llm_custom_prompt_no_text: The template has no {text}, so the line is added at the end.
transl.llm_preview_sample: Nice to meet you! Are you coming to the event tonight?
transl.llm_preview_hint: What the model receives for this line with the current language pair, glossary and background. Earlier lines are added while translation runs.
transl.llm_reasoning_hint: Translation models (Hy-MT2, MiLMMT, TranslateGemma) do not reason: keep Model default. For thinking models, None or Minimal keeps captions fast.
transl.llm_timeout_hint: Partial captions use a shorter limit. With automatic routing, the time per engine applies as well.
transl.llm_stream_hint: The first words of a translation appear while the model is still writing.
transl.llm_interim_hint: Translates partial captions too, which costs more GPU time or cloud quota.
transl.llm_transport_hint: Automatic sends cloud requests directly and routes servers on your network through Sigil, which also reaches local servers that block the app window.
transl.deepl_desc: DeepL API Free translates 500,000 characters a month at no cost. Create a key at deepl.com (API plans); Free keys end in :fx.
transl.deepl_usage_failed: Could not read the usage. Check the key, the plan and the connection.
transl.deepl_lists_builtin: DeepL's language list could not be loaded, so Sigil's built-in list is used.
transl.deepl_formality_unsupported: DeepL has no formality setting for {{language}}, so it is ignored.
transl.deepl_model_hint: "Best quality only" fails for languages DeepL's newest model does not cover; "when available" falls back instead.
transl.deepl_context_hint: DeepL does not count context against the character quota.
transl.deepl_interim_hint: Every partial caption counts against the monthly quota.
transl.bergamot_desc: Firefox Translations runs on the processor with no video memory and no internet. Each direction is a small download (about 17–60 MB); pairs without English go through English.
transl.bergamot_pivot: No direct model for this pair: it is translated through English with two models.
transl.bergamot_unknown_source: Choose a source language to see which models this pair needs. With the source set to automatic, install the models for each language you speak.
transl.bergamot_interim_hint: Fast enough to translate partial captions on most PCs.
transl.mt_threads_hint: More threads translate faster but take processor time from games.
transl.nllb_desc: NLLB-200 translates between about 200 languages on the processor, with no internet. Best for languages the other engines do not cover.
transl.nllb_model_hint: 600M is faster (about 0.9 GB); 1.3B translates better but needs more memory and time.
transl.nllb_beam_hint: Wider beams can give better full translations but take longer. Partial captions always use 1.
transl.nllb_interim_hint: Translating partial captions keeps the processor busy while you speak.
transl.libre_ltengine_hint: LTEngine runs Gemma 3 models on your PC behind the LibreTranslate API. Start it with ltengine (add -m gemma3-12b for a larger model). It detects the source language itself.
transl.libre_probe_failed: No LibreTranslate-compatible server answered at this address yet.
transl.libre_auto_source_hint: The server detects the source language of every line.
transl.libre_auto_detect_hint: Asks the server for the language of each line first and falls back to the source language above.
transl.llm_bundled_desktop_only: Sigil's model server runs only in the desktop app.
transl.error_backend_unavailable: This translation provider is not available in this build yet.
transl.glossary_shadowed: An earlier entry for this term is used instead, so this one is never sent.
transl.glossary_shadowed_pair: For {{pair}}, an earlier entry for this term is used instead of this one.
transl.glossary_shadowed_spelling: When a line spells the term exactly "{{spelling}}", an earlier entry for it is used instead of this one.
transl.glossary_shadowed_pair_spelling: For {{pair}}, when a line spells the term exactly "{{spelling}}", an earlier entry for it is used instead of this one.
transl.glossary_unknown_language: Not a language code: {{list}}. This term is sent only while a line's language is unknown; pick a language under "Languages and case".
transl.glossary_import_ignored_columns: Extra columns that are not language codes were left out ({{count}}); those terms apply to any language.
transl.glossary_paste_help: One term per line: term and translation separated by a tab (as copied from a spreadsheet), "=", "->" or a comma. Optional third and fourth tab columns limit it to a source and target language code. Lines starting with # are skipped; put a term that starts with # in quotes.
transl.interim_cpu_hint: Off for now: the local translator runs on the processor, where live partial translations take about 4 cores next to a game. Tick the box to turn them on; the final lines are always translated.

transform.title: Rewrite
transform.system_prompt_placeholder: Example: Rewrite the input text to be more professional, correcting any grammar mistakes.
transform.tokens_reasoning_hint: Thinking models spend part of the token limit on reasoning, so a low limit can leave no room for the reply. Lower effort answers faster. Not every model accepts every level: keep "Model default" if the provider reports an error.
transform.live_settings_hint: Key, URL, model, prompt and limits apply from the next sentence; no restart needed.
transform.context_history_hint: ✱ Sends your previous sentences to the model for better context. Uses slightly more tokens.
transform.error_key_missing: Enter an API key for {{provider}} first.
transform.error_url_missing: Enter the API URL of your OpenAI-compatible server first.
transform.error_timeout: Rewrite got no reply within {{seconds}} s, so the original text was sent instead.
transform.error_rate_limited: The provider is rate limiting requests, so the original text is sent until it recovers.
transform.error_truncated: The model's reply hit the max output tokens limit before producing any text, so the original text was sent. Raise "Max output tokens" or lower the reasoning effort.
transform.error_empty: The model returned no text, so the original text was sent instead.
transform.error_request: Rewrite request failed (HTTP {{status}}): {{error}}. The original text was sent instead.
transform.field_fence_input: Treat speech as text to rewrite
transform.fence_input_hint: Recommended. Each line is sent inside <text> tags with a note that it is text to rewrite, so the model does not answer spoken questions or follow instructions someone says. Turn this off only if your instructions should make the model reply to what you say.
transform.gemini_hint: Create a free API key in Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com). Flash-Lite models answer fastest and have the most generous free limits.
transform.check_ok: Connected: {{n}} models available, including this one.
transform.check_ok_empty: Connected. The server did not list its models.
transform.check_ok_model_missing: Connected, but "{{model}}" is not one of the server's {{n}} models. Check the model name.
transform.transport_hint: Automatic sends cloud requests directly and routes servers on your network through Sigil, which also reaches local servers that block browser requests (Ollama, LM Studio). Change it only if a server cannot be reached.
transform.error_unauthorized: The provider rejected the API key ({{error}}), so the original text was sent. Check the key.
transform.error_network: Rewrite could not reach the server ({{error}}), so the original text was sent.
transform.stream_hint_until_next: Captions bound to the synced source ("Rewrite: original text (synced)") fill in word by word as the reply arrives, until you start the next sentence; the line then waits for the finished reply. TTS, the chatbox and the "Rewritten text" source still get only the finished line. Servers that cannot stream get plain requests automatically.
transform.intro: Rewrites each finished sentence with a language model, using your instructions (fix grammar, change tone, shorten). It runs next to Speech to Text; start both. Choose "Rewritten text" as the text source of a caption, Text to Speech or the VRChat chatbox to use it.

vrc.textbox_paginate_desc: The chatbox shows at most 144 characters. Longer text is sent as numbered pages, one after the other, instead of being cut off.
vrc.textbox_interval_desc: VRChat ignores chatbox messages that arrive less than about 1.3 seconds apart, so messages and pages wait their turn. Short messages that are still waiting are sent together.
vrc.textbox_commit_turn_end_desc: When you pause in the middle of a thought, the sentence waits and goes out together with the rest, so the chatbox gets whole thoughts instead of fragments.
vrc.textbox_commit_turn_end_translation: Translated text already waits for the end of your turn (translation setting "Wait until you finish speaking"), so it is not held a second time.
vrc.textbox_commit_turn_end_needs_smart_turn: Needs "Detect when you finish speaking (Smart Turn)" in the speech-to-text settings (Built-in). Until then every sentence is sent at once.
vrc.mute_sync: Mute captions when I mute in VRChat
vrc.mute_sync_desc: Muting your microphone in VRChat also mutes Sigil's speech-to-text, and unmuting turns it back on. A mute you set in Sigil yourself stays until you lift it.
vrc.osc_query_desc: Sigil listens on a free port and tells VRChat where, so it never clashes with other OSC apps that use port 9001. Turn this off to listen on a fixed port instead.
vrc.osc_listen_port_remote_desc: VRChat runs on another PC: start it there with the launch option --osc=9000:THIS-PC-IP:PORT, using this PC's address and the port above.
vrc.receiver_needs_enable: Turn on the VRChat integration above to listen to VRChat.
vrc.receiver_listening_oscquery: Listening on port {{port}}. VRChat finds Sigil by itself.
vrc.receiver_no_messages: Nothing received from VRChat yet. Check that OSC is on in VRChat (Action menu » Options » OSC » Enable).
vrc.receiver_mic_muted_sync: VRChat microphone muted: captions are muted too.
vrc.tags_enable: Send emotion and sound tags to VRChat
vrc.tags_desc: The SenseVoice model of speech-to-text on this PC hears how you sound (happy, sad, ...) and sounds such as laughter. Sigil can pass them to your avatar as Int parameters and show them as emoji in the chatbox. Other speech recognizers send no tags.
vrc.tags_emotion_values: Values: 0 neutral, 1 happy, 2 sad, 3 angry, 4 fearful, 5 disgusted, 6 surprised.
vrc.tags_event_values: Values: 0 none, 1 laughter, 2 applause, 3 crying, 4 cough, 5 sneeze, 6 breathing, 7 music.
vrc.tags_reset_desc: Leave a parameter name empty to not send it. 0 keeps the last value until the next tagged sentence.

voice_changer.vram_note: Voice conversion can use a lot of GPU time alongside VRChat or OBS. Prefer a WebSocket server on another PC or GPU, or use built-in mode to save resources. See scripts/neural-sidecar/README.md.
voice_changer.title: Voice changer
voice_changer.sidecar_ws_hint: Use ws:// or wss:// (for example ws://127.0.0.1:8765). Run your converter server first; see scripts/neural-sidecar/README.md.
voice_changer.sidecar_pitch_note: Your WebSocket server supplies the main conversion; Pitch and the other Sound sliders still process audio after it returns.
voice_changer.sidecar_postprocess_divider: After WebSocket or ONNX (pitch, brightness, smoothing)
voice_changer.onnx_model_hint: Float32 in/out; choose a .onnx file. Use the repo identity model to test the path. Sigil adjusts chunk shape when it does not match your mic.
voice_changer.oversampling_hint: More steps per analysis window usually means smoother pitch and higher CPU. Use 1 or 2 if the voice changer stutters.
voice_changer.tips_body: Start turns processing on; Stop turns it off. Pitch always uses the phase vocoder (built-in on the mic, or on WebSocket/ONNX output). Brightness adjusts high/low balance, not full formant modeling. Window length and oversampling trade CPU for quality; if it stutters, shorten the window or try oversampling 1, 2, or 4. Changing chunk size, buffer ms, output devices, or monitor device while running restarts the voice changer. Echo cancellation and noise suppression are not built in—use your OS, mic software, or OBS filters if needed.
voice_changer.onnx_postprocess_note: The ONNX model runs first; Pitch, brightness, and phase-vocoder settings then refine the output.
voice_changer.onnx_browse_unavailable: File browse is available in the desktop app.
voice_changer.chunk_hint: Larger chunks add delay but can stabilize conversion; ONNX models need a compatible fixed shape—Sigil adapts when possible. Changing chunk restarts processing.
voice_changer.buffer_truncate_hint: When the queued tail is consistently quiet, drop backlog toward the minimum prefill to reduce delay (similar to VCClient worklet truncation).
voice_changer.quick_presets_hint: One-tap character presets; use the controls above for fine tuning.
voice_changer.monitor_hint: Send processed audio to a second output (e.g. headphones) while the main output goes to a virtual cable for VRChat or OBS. Uses the same buffer settings as the main output; gain is independent of main output gain.
voice_changer.sidecar_ws_info:
Use ws:// or wss:// (for example ws://127.0.0.1:8765). Start your converter before Sigil; see scripts/neural-sidecar/README.md.

Your server supplies the main conversion; the Sound section can still shift pitch, brightness, and smoothing on the returned audio.
voice_changer.section_how_it_works_info: Pick built-in processing, a WebSocket converter, a local ONNX file, or RVC (bring-your-own ONNX slot). WebSocket, ONNX, and RVC handle the main voice change; the Sound section can still adjust pitch, brightness, and smoothing on the result.
voice_changer.section_timing_buffer_info: Low latency vs Stable only changes the playback cushion (prefill / max queue). Chunk size and exact millisecond values live under Advanced. This is separate from the RVC Quality profile.
voice_changer.section_sound_info: Pitch and brightness apply in every mode. In Built-in they are the main effect; in RVC / ONNX / WebSocket they refine the converted audio.
voice_changer.section_devices_info: Main output is what viewers or VRChat hear. Monitor is an optional second output (for example headphones) while the main device stays on a virtual cable.
voice_changer.section_advanced_info: Chunk size, exact buffer milliseconds, and silence trim. Prefer Playback feel above unless you need custom values.
voice_changer.onnx_files_info:
Float32 in/out; pick a .onnx file. Use the repo identity model to test the path. Sigil adjusts chunk shape when it does not match your mic.

The model does the main conversion; Pitch and the other Sound controls still run afterward on its output.
voice_changer.onnx_ep_help: Registers ONNX Runtime execution providers for the voice model in order (GPU then CPU fallback). CPU is the most compatible. CUDA requires NVIDIA drivers; DirectML is Windows-only. Does not affect mic or speaker routing.
voice_changer.wip_banner_body: Voice changer is still evolving — settings hot-swap when possible; some changes restart the engine.
voice_changer.toast_error_onnx: Voice changer (ONNX): conversion failed; that audio was muted. {{message}}
voice_changer.toast_error_sidecar: Voice changer (WebSocket): conversion failed; that audio was muted. {{message}}
voice_changer.toast_error_sidecar_length: Voice changer (WebSocket): wrong chunk size; using dry input. {{message}}
voice_changer.hot_swap_note: Changing mode, devices, chunk size, or model path reconnects the audio pipeline in place (no app restart). Timing buffer sliders apply while running.
voice_changer.rvc_quality_banner: Quality uses more GPU/VRAM and can contend with OBS and games. Prefer Streamer while streaming, or encode with NVENC so the game GPU stays free for RVC.
voice_changer.vram_cap_cuda_only: Only applies when the execution provider is CUDA. The cap is per ONNX session (HuBERT, generator and pitch extractor each get it), so total VRAM use can reach about three times the cap.
voice_changer.debug_captured: Debug snapshot written to the developer console.
voice_changer.section_rvc_bases_info: Optional if files live under AppData/com.sigil.app/voice-changer/base/ (hubert_base.onnx, fcpe.onnx, rmvpe.onnx). Empty paths auto-resolve from that folder or the slot.
voice_changer.section_rvc_tuning_info: Extra context and crossfade trade latency for stability; the engine restarts when you release the slider or leave the field. Crossfade cannot be longer than one processing chunk, so its maximum follows the chunk size (about 10 ms at 512 samples). Index rate blends in the slot's FAISS .index file (standard RVC IVF-Flat exports load); 0 turns it off. Protect keeps breaths and voiceless consonants clear (lower is stronger; 0.5 turns it off).
voice_changer.section_rvc_expert_info: RVC has its own execution provider, separate from ONNX mode; GPU providers fall back to CPU. CUDA requires NVIDIA drivers; DirectML is Windows-only. GPU device index picks the CUDA or DirectML adapter (0 = first GPU). VRAM cap limits CUDA memory only, per ONNX session (HuBERT, generator and pitch extractor). Speaker ID selects the voice in multi-speaker models. Does not affect mic or speaker routing.
voice_changer.section_tone_vocoder_info: Analysis window and oversampling only apply to the Built-in phase vocoder. Leave defaults unless you need more smoothness or lower latency.
voice_changer.toast_error_worker_panic: Voice changer stopped after an internal error. Start it again; if it keeps happening, report it. {{message}}
voice_changer.ep_fallback: {{requested}} is not available, so the voice model runs on {{active}}.
voice_changer.toast_ep_fallback: Voice changer: {{requested}} is not available, so it runs on {{active}}. Reason: {{reason}}
voice_changer.metrics_starting: Starting: opening devices and loading the model…
voice_changer.metrics_slow_warn: Conversion is slower than real time, so audio is being skipped. Pick a lighter profile or pitch extractor, a larger chunk size, or a GPU execution provider.
voice_changer.metrics_spikes_warn: Some blocks take longer than real time (p99), so expect an occasional skip. A larger chunk size, a lighter profile or the Protect voice priority helps.
voice_changer.metrics_dropping_warn: The voice changer is falling behind: audio older than the latency budget is skipped so your voice stays in time.
voice_changer.metrics_underrun_warn: Playback ran dry. Choose More delay under Playback feel, or raise the output prefill under Advanced.
voice_changer.latency_budget_info:
The most captured audio that may wait for conversion. When the voice changer falls behind (a GPU spike, a busy game), audio older than this is skipped instead of piling up, so your voice never drifts further and further behind.

Lower keeps the delay short but skips more under load; higher skips less but can add delay after a hiccup. 300 ms suits most PCs. Applies right away, in every mode (it is also how long Sigil waits for a WebSocket converter).
voice_changer.worker_priority_info:
How the voice changer shares the PC with your game and OBS.

Automatic: normal priority when the model runs on the GPU, lower priority when it runs on the CPU, so a CPU voice does not cost game frames.
Protect game FPS: always lower priority. The game wins; the voice may skip under heavy load.
Protect voice: normal priority and never throttled by Windows power saving. Fewer skips; the game may lose a few frames on a busy CPU.

Applies right away. Sigil never asks for administrator rights.
voice_changer.aux_mic_gate_info: Text-to-speech sent through the voice changer is mixed with your microphone before conversion. Lower the microphone turns it down by about 12 dB while TTS plays; Mute the microphone silences it so only the TTS voice is converted. Applies right away.
voice_changer.rvc_voices_empty: No voices in {{path}} yet. Put each voice in its own folder there (gen.onnx and an optional .index file) to pick it from a list, or choose any folder above.
voice_changer.rvc_slot_help:
A voice is a folder with gen.onnx (or model.onnx) and, optionally, the model's FAISS .index file (for example added_IVF256_Flat_nprobe_1.index) for Index rate. manifest.json is optional: without it Sigil infers the sample rate and features from the model, and warns if it has to guess. Voices in %AppData%/com.sigil.app/voice-changer/models/ appear in the Voice list.

Sigil keeps each voice's pitch, brightness, index rate, protect, pitch extractor and speaker ID in a slot.json file in its folder, so they come back when you pick the voice again.

Put shared HuBERT/ContentVec and FCPE under %AppData%/com.sigil.app/voice-changer/base/ (hubert_base.onnx, fcpe.onnx) or set paths below. First bring-up: Streamer + CPU + dio or fcpe; leave index at 0. Prefer 40 kHz exports. On 4-core PCs use OBS NVENC/QSV/AMF.
voice_changer.pitch_extractor_cpu_note: {{name}} needs a GPU execution provider. While RVC runs on the CPU, fcpe is used instead.
voice_changer.rvc_voice_consent_body: RVC makes you sound like the voice model you load. Only use voices whose owners agreed to it, and never use a converted voice to impersonate or deceive anyone.
voice_changer.rvc_voice_consent_ack: I will only use voices I have permission to use
voice_changer.toast_params_failed: Voice changer settings were not applied: {{message}}
voice_changer.toast_error_sidecar_connect: Voice changer (WebSocket): could not connect to the converter. {{message}}
voice_changer.toast_error_onnx_load: Voice changer (ONNX): the model could not be loaded. {{message}}
voice_changer.section_voices_info:
Your RVC voices. Drop .pth or .zip voices (RVC WebUI, Applio, Mangio and w-okada exports) on the import box, or pick them with Import. Sigil converts them once for its own engine. Bring-your-own ONNX voices (a folder with gen.onnx) keep working: put them in the voices folder, or choose Other folder.

Picking another voice while the voice changer runs switches without a restart: the new voice loads in the background and fades in.
voice_changer.voices_desktop_only: Voices are managed in the desktop app.
voice_changer.voice_delete_confirm: Delete “{{name}}” and its files? This cannot be undone.
voice_changer.voice_delete_in_use: The voice changer is using this voice. Stop it or pick another voice first.
voice_changer.voice_merge_help: Blends two imported voices of the same model type into a new voice. The slider sets how much of each voice goes in.
voice_changer.voice_merge_none: No other imported voice has the same model type and content encoder.
voice_changer.voice_models_reason: This voice and your pitch setting use:
voice_changer.voice_no_pitch_note: This voice was trained without pitch, so it needs no pitch extractor and ignores the pitch settings.
voice_changer.import_ignored: Only .pth and .zip voices (and an .index next to one .pth) can be imported. Skipped: {{files}}
voice_changer.import_index_unpaired: An .index file is used only when you drop it together with exactly one .pth. Voices inside a .zip bring their own index.
voice_changer.import_error_io: The file or folder could not be read or written.
voice_changer.import_error_job: The request could not be done.
voice_changer.import_error_not_a_checkpoint: This file is not an RVC voice checkpoint.
voice_changer.import_error_legacy_format: This is an old-style PyTorch file. Save it again with a newer RVC or Applio, then import it.
voice_changer.import_error_torchscript: This is a TorchScript export, not an RVC voice checkpoint.
voice_changer.import_error_archive_rejected: The .zip file was refused (too large, too many files, or unsafe paths).
voice_changer.import_error_ambiguous_archive: The .zip file holds more than one voice. Import each .pth on its own.
voice_changer.import_error_pickle_rejected: The file contains code Sigil does not run, so it was refused for your safety.
voice_changer.import_error_missing_tensor: The voice is missing weights (it may be a training checkpoint, not a finished voice).
voice_changer.import_error_shape_mismatch: The voice's weights do not match any model type Sigil knows.
voice_changer.import_error_non_finite: The voice's weights contain invalid numbers.
voice_changer.import_error_unsupported_model: This kind of voice is not supported yet.
voice_changer.import_error_no_template: Sigil has no engine template for this model type.
voice_changer.import_error_layout_invalid: An engine template of this build is damaged. Reinstall Sigil.
voice_changer.import_error_session: The converted voice could not be loaded for its test run.
voice_changer.import_error_time_limit: The import took too long and was stopped.
voice_changer.import_error_precision_refused: The voice does not convert accurately enough at this precision.
voice_changer.starter_body: One click installs a ready-to-use voice and the models the voice changer needs. You can also drop your own .pth or .zip voice below.
voice_changer.hotkeys_info: Global shortcuts that work while Sigil is in the background (for example in VRChat): start or stop the voice changer, step through your voices, or jump straight to a chosen voice. Switching voices while it runs has no gap.
voice_changer.hotkeys_note: A voice hotkey also switches the voice changer to RVC voices.
voice_changer.hotkey_no_voices: Voice changer: there are no voices to switch to.
voice_changer.hotkey_no_voice_assigned: Voice changer: no voice is set for this hotkey.
voice_changer.hotkey_consent_needed: Voice changer: open the voice changer panel and confirm the voice permission notice to start RVC.
voice_changer.section_preset_info: A starting point for the engine: execution provider, pitch extractor, index and context. Autotune (under Benchmark and tuning) can then pick the fastest settings that stay smooth on this PC.
voice_changer.rvc_profile_info: Streamer runs on the CPU and leaves the GPU to your game and OBS. Low latency and Quality use the GPU. Studio-TRT uses NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX: the first start builds optimized engines (up to a minute), later starts load them from the cache.
voice_changer.rvc_profile_studio_trt_unavailable: TensorRT-RTX is not available on this PC, so Studio-TRT runs its Quality settings on CUDA.
voice_changer.section_voice_settings_info: These are saved with the selected voice (as are its pitch and formant), so each voice keeps its own. They apply while the voice changer runs.
voice_changer.pitch_extractor_info: How your pitch is tracked. RMVPE is the most accurate (GPU). FCPE is fast. SwiftF0 is the lightest for the CPU. CREPE tiny and PESTO are other neural trackers. Fusion combines SwiftF0's voicing with RMVPE's pitch to avoid octave jumps. Dio is classic signal processing.
voice_changer.pitch_extractor_runs_as: {{name}} is not available in this build, so {{run}} runs instead.
voice_changer.f0_range_info: Speech tracks 50 to 1100 Hz. Singing reaches up to 2.5 kHz for high notes; use it for singing voices.
voice_changer.speaker: Speaker
voice_changer.index_rate_info: How much of the voice's own timbre is pulled from its index file. Higher sounds more like the voice but can blur words.
voice_changer.index_rate_no_index: This voice has no index file, so the index rate has no effect.
voice_changer.protect_info: Keeps breaths and consonants from your own voice so words stay clear. Lower protects more; 0.5 turns it off.
voice_changer.rms_mix_info: Where the loudness of the converted voice comes from. 1 keeps the model's own dynamics; lower values follow how loud you actually speak.
voice_changer.noise_scale_info: How much natural variation the voice model adds (its noise scale). Lower is steadier and flatter; the default suits most voices. Imported voices only.
voice_changer.formant_semitones_info: Moves the voice's resonances up or down without changing its pitch: a lower formant sounds bigger and deeper, a higher one smaller and brighter. Saved with the voice.
voice_changer.formant_tilt_rvc_note: While Formant is not 0, Brightness has no effect in RVC mode.
voice_changer.block_ms_info: How much new audio the engine converts at a time. Smaller blocks lower the delay but cost more; Auto follows the processing chunk size under Latency. Imported voices only.
voice_changer.template_only_note: Applies to imported voices; bring-your-own ONNX voices ignore it.
voice_changer.section_engine_info: Expert settings of the Sigil Voice Engine. Leave them on Auto unless you are testing: Auto uses what Sigil's benchmark measured to be best for each preset. Changes here restart the voice changer.
voice_changer.rvc_ep_info: Where the voice runs. CUDA and TensorRT-RTX need an NVIDIA GPU; DirectML works on any GPU. The high-priority DirectML queue keeps your voice smooth while a game uses the GPU. If a GPU provider cannot start, the voice runs on the next one and the reason is shown.
voice_changer.ep_runs_as: {{name}} is not available on this PC, so the voice runs on {{base}}.
voice_changer.trt_first_start_note: The first start builds TensorRT engines for this voice (up to a minute); later starts load them from the cache.
voice_changer.precision_info: Auto uses half precision on the GPU where Sigil's tests show it is accurate, and full precision elsewhere. fp32 is always full precision; fp16 forces half precision (less VRAM, faster).
voice_changer.precision_runs_as: {{name}} is not available in this build, so {{run}} is used.
voice_changer.levers_info: Each lever is one of the engine's techniques. Auto uses the benchmark-proven default of the preset; On asks for it (it runs when this build and the execution provider support it); Off always uses the proven classic path.
voice_changer.levers_legacy_note: Bring-your-own ONNX voices use only noise anchoring, partial decode (when the export allows it) and the governor. Import the voice's .pth to use every lever.
voice_changer.levers_restart_note: The status shows what the running voice really uses.
voice_changer.lever_info_partial_decode: Decodes only the audio that is played, not the whole context, so more context costs almost nothing.
voice_changer.lever_info_anchored_noise: Uses the same model noise for the same moment on every block, so overlapping blocks match and joins stay clean.
voice_changer.lever_info_nsf_phase0: Keeps the voice's excitation continuous from block to block instead of restarting it, which removes buzzy seams.
voice_changer.lever_info_f0_cache: Tracks pitch only for the new audio and reuses the rest, which keeps larger context cheap.
voice_changer.lever_info_gpu_knn: Searches the voice's index exactly on the GPU instead of approximately on the CPU.
voice_changer.lever_info_io_binding: Keeps the model's inputs and outputs on the GPU between blocks (fewer copies).
voice_changer.lever_info_cuda_graphs: Records each block's GPU work once and replays it, which removes most launch overhead (NVIDIA).
voice_changer.lever_info_gpu_priority: Runs the voice on a high-priority GPU queue so a busy game delays it less.
voice_changer.lever_info_governor: When the PC is busy, lowers quality step by step (index off, less context, lighter pitch tracking) instead of stuttering, and raises it again when things calm down.
voice_changer.silence_db_info: Below this level the engine skips conversion (no GPU work while you are quiet). Raise it if room noise keeps the voice changer busy; lower it if quiet words are cut.
voice_changer.hot_slots_info: How many voices stay loaded for instant switching (hotkeys). Each extra voice uses a little more memory; the content encoder and pitch models are shared.
voice_changer.hot_slots_cpu_note: On the CPU, extra loaded voices use system memory instead of VRAM.
voice_changer.vram_budget_info: The most GPU memory the voice changer may use for loaded voices. 0 = automatic (leaves room for your game and other Sigil features).
voice_changer.denoiser_info: Removes background noise (fans, keyboard, room) from the voice changer's input before conversion. Speech-to-text still hears the raw microphone.
voice_changer.denoiser_runs_as: {{name}} is not available in this build, so {{run}} runs instead.
voice_changer.denoiser_runs_off: {{name}} is not available in this build, so no noise removal runs.
voice_changer.metrics_governor_warn: The PC is busy, so the voice changer lowered its quality to keep up. It raises it again when the load drops.
voice_changer.trt_building_hint: Building TensorRT engines for this voice. This happens once (up to a minute); later starts load them from the cache.

voice_changer.lookahead_ms_info: How much future audio the engine looks at before it outputs a block. More lookahead gives cleaner joins between blocks and steadier pitch and voicing, and adds exactly that much delay. Quality uses 20 ms; Low latency uses none. Imported voices on CUDA or the CPU; it is not used yet while the voice runs on DirectML.
voice_changer.family_about_ddsp_svc: A singing voice trained with DDSP-SVC 6.3. It follows your pitch from E2 up to D#7 without clamping, so vibrato and high notes come through.
voice_changer.family_about_sigil_zs: Sounds like any voice from a short clip in your voice library, with no training (Seed-VC real-time, inside Sigil's engine). Needs a GPU.
voice_changer.family_about_meanvc: Zero-shot conversion from a library clip that runs on the CPU and leaves the GPU free. It was trained on Mandarin speech, so other languages may sound less natural.
voice_changer.family_about_sovits: A so-vits-svc 4.1 voice exported to ONNX. It uses your pitch and the shared content encoder, like an RVC voice.
voice_changer.family_about_sidecar_v2: A voice engine that runs as a separate program on this PC (X-VC, StreamVoiceAnon, seed-vc-realtime or your own server) and talks to Sigil over a local WebSocket.
voice_changer.family_info_ddsp_svc: DDSP-SVC renders a singing voice with a fixed number of flow steps per block. Singing and Singing (fast) use 100 ms blocks with 10 or 5 steps; Upstream uses upstream's 500 ms window with 20 steps, which adds delay. Turn on singing mode so the pitch range reaches D#7, and use CREPE, SwiftF0 or fusion for the pitch: RMVPE and FCPE miss the highest notes. It runs on CUDA or DirectML, with at least a 70 ms output buffer.
voice_changer.family_info_sigil_zs: Sigil-ZS converts toward a reference voice from your voice library. Low delay and Lean use 100 ms blocks (about 250 ms of delay on a fast GPU, with the 80-95 ms output buffer these voices need); Upstream uses 180 ms blocks (about 350 ms). The metrics show the delay you actually get. A clean 5-10 s clip of one speaker with no music, with at least 4 s of speech, gives the best result.
voice_changer.family_info_meanvc: MeanVC2 generates the voice every 80 ms (or every 160 ms for a little less CPU and more delay) with one or two mean-flow steps at 16 kHz. It always runs on the CPU, whatever execution provider is selected. It is experimental: compare it with an RVC voice on the Streamer preset before relying on it.
voice_changer.family_info_sovits: so-vits-svc voices use the shared content encoder and the pitch extractor you pick. Cluster / index mix blends the voice's retrieval features when the voice ships them.
voice_changer.family_info_sidecar_v2: Sidecar voices hand each block to a program on this PC and wait at most the per-block timeout (by default the latency budget); a block that comes back late is dropped, so a stalled engine never stalls your voice. X-VC and StreamVoiceAnon need a GPU with 12 GB or more. Only ws:// addresses on this PC are allowed.
voice_changer.family_experimental_note: Experimental: its quality and delay are still being measured. Compare it with your other voices before using it live.
