voice_changer.family_ddsp_preset_info: How long each block is and how many flow steps it gets. Fewer steps are faster; a longer window is smoother but adds delay.
voice_changer.family_ddsp_preset_upstream_gui: Upstream (500 ms window, 20 steps; more delay)
voice_changer.family_ddsp_steps_info: Flow steps per block (1-50). Empty uses the preset's.
voice_changer.family_ddsp_t_start_info: Where the flow starts between the DDSP rendering (1) and noise (0). Higher keeps more of the DDSP rendering and needs fewer steps. Empty uses 0.7, upstream's default.
voice_changer.family_zs_preset_info: Low delay and Lean use 100 ms blocks (about 250 ms of delay on a fast GPU); Upstream uses 180 ms blocks (about 350 ms) and more steps. Lean skips guidance and listens to a shorter part of the reference to run faster. The metrics show the delay you actually get.
voice_changer.family_zs_preset_sigil_low: Low delay (100 ms blocks, 6 steps, guidance)
voice_changer.family_zs_preset_sigil_lean: Lean (100 ms blocks, 4 steps, no guidance)
voice_changer.family_zs_preset_upstream_readme: Upstream (180 ms blocks, 10 steps; more delay)
voice_changer.family_zs_steps_info: Diffusion steps per block (1-30). More steps sound cleaner and cost more GPU time. Empty uses the preset's.
voice_changer.family_zs_cfg_rate_info: Classifier-free guidance (0-1): how strongly the voice is pushed toward the reference. 0 turns it off and halves the work per step. Empty uses the preset's.
voice_changer.family_zs_prompt_s_info: How many seconds of the reference clip the model listens to (0.5-10). Longer captures more of the voice and costs more per block. Empty uses the preset's.
voice_changer.family_zs_fp16_vocoder_info: Runs the HiFT vocoder in fp16. Auto uses what the benchmark found best.
voice_changer.family_zs_fp16_note: Half precision is faster but changes the sound: the fp16 DiT does not match the full-precision model's audio. Keep it off unless your GPU cannot keep up.
voice_changer.family_meanvc_steps_info: Mean-flow steps per tick: 1 is faster, 2 sounds better.
voice_changer.family_meanvc_tick_info: How often the voice is generated: 80 ms gives less delay; 160 ms uses a little less CPU but adds delay, and it always plays with at least the Stable output buffer (80 / 150 ms). To save CPU without the extra delay, use 1 step instead.
voice_changer.family_meanvc_tick_160: 160 ms (a little less CPU, more delay)
voice_changer.family_sovits_cluster_ratio_info: Blends the voice's retrieval features (its cluster model or index) into your content when the voice ships them: higher sounds more like the voice, lower keeps your articulation. 0 is off.
voice_changer.family_sidecar_recipe_info: Which program converts your voice. The recipes start it for you from a Python environment where the engine is installed; Custom server connects to a protocol v2 server you run yourself. Everything stays on this PC.
voice_changer.family_sidecar_recipe_custom_about: Connects to your own server at a ws:// address on this PC (see scripts/neural-sidecar/PROTOCOL_V2.md).

voice_changer.family_formant_hidden_note: This voice ignores Formant, but Formant is still set to {{value}} st (from another voice), which turns Brightness off.
voice_changer.lookahead_ms_info_v2: How much future audio the engine looks at before it outputs a block. More lookahead gives cleaner joins between blocks and steadier pitch and voicing, and adds exactly that much delay. Quality uses 20 ms; Low latency uses none. Imported voices only. On DirectML it is used when the content encoder runs at a fixed shape (the default); if it cannot, the engine says so under the engine levers and runs without it.
voice_changer.output_cushion_info: Audio the output keeps queued so a late block does not leave a gap. Fixed holds the output prefill from the buffer settings and is the safe choice. Adaptive starts there, watches how late your blocks really are for about half a minute, then gives back what the stream never needs, during pauses in your speech first. It never holds more than the prefill, and if the output runs dry once it grows the cushion again, remembers how much it needed and stops shrinking for a while. It is experimental: while other programs keep the PC very busy it can still run dry now and then.
voice_changer.output_cushion_adaptive_live: Holding {{ms}} ms now, at most {{max}} ms.
voice_changer.output_cushion_adaptive_note: Starts at {{max}} ms and shrinks after the first half minute of speech and pauses.
voice_changer.device_block_info: How much audio is handed to the voice at a time. As set uses the chunk size above. Divides the engine block uses 10 ms blocks (a size that divides the engine block, so each model block finishes exactly when its audio is due and the output buffer holds back less). Lowers the delay by roughly 15 ms at 40 ms engine blocks. Imported voices only.
voice_changer.device_block_template_only: Only imported (Sigil engine) voices use this; this voice keeps the chunk size.
voice_changer.sola_search_ms_info: How far the engine searches around each block join for the best-matching position, in ms. Automatic is half the crossfade. A narrow window helps imported voices whose blocks already agree, and a 0 ms window joins at the nominal point. Changing it restarts a running engine.
voice_changer.content_context_ms_info: How much earlier speech the content encoder hears before the block, in ms. Automatic is the preset's window. More gives the encoder real context at word starts (the model was trained on seconds of speech) and costs a little quality elsewhere in our tests; it does not add delay. Imported voices only. Changing it restarts a running engine.
voice_changer.lever_info_content_norm: Opt-in. Normalises the speech features with running statistics of your recent speech instead of each short window's own, which raised voice similarity by about 0.01 in our tests and costs a little spectral accuracy. It needs the content encoder's streaming variant, which is not part of the downloads yet; without it the engine switches this off and says so.
voice_changer.lever_info_f0_decode: Experimental. Decides each new pitch frame together with the frames before it, which can correct octave jumps. On our test speech it did not improve pitch accuracy and slightly lowered voice similarity, so it is off by default. Works with the RMVPE pitch method. Not used for singing.
voice_changer.device_block_not_applied: Not applied here: the engine block follows the chunk size, or no whole 10 ms block fits this sample rate, so the chunk size above is used. Running {{ms}} ms blocks.
voice_changer.output_buffer_raised: This voice plays with at least {{prefill}} / {{queue}} ms of output buffer (prefill / max queue), more than the {{stored_prefill}} / {{stored_queue}} ms set here: it converts a long block in one call while the output keeps playing. Your numbers are kept for other voices; a buffer you typed yourself is raised only when it cannot hold the voice's calls.
voice_changer.rvc_streamer_few_cores_note: Block size {{current}} ms is shorter than the {{block}} ms that Auto takes on this PC ({{cores}} physical cores). Streamer converts on the processor, and a short block falls behind there while a game is running: in Sigil's test, 120 ms skipped about a tenth to a fifth of the speech on PCs with 4 to 6 cores, and the voice arrived about half a second late. Auto, or {{block}} ms or more, dropped at most half a percent of the speech in the tests on 4- and 6-core PCs, at a larger delay; Low latency (GPU) uses the graphics card instead.

others.status_restarting: Other players' captions stopped ({{detail}}). Restarting in {{seconds}} s…
others.error_desktop_only: Other players' captions work in the desktop app only.
others.error_unsupported: This Windows version can't capture one program (it needs Windows 11 or Windows 10 build 20348 or newer). Turn on the default-output option or pick an output device.
others.error_no_engine: No speech model is available for this language on this PC. Choose another language or hardware setting.
others.error_models_missing: Download the speech models in the Other players panel first: {{list}}
others.error_not_installed: {{model}} is missing. Download it in the Other players panel or in Models & Runtimes.
others.error_gave_up: Other players' captions stopped after {{attempts}} failed restarts. Last error: {{detail}}
others.error_plan: Could not check the sound source.
others.error_stopped_elsewhere: Another start replaced the other players' recognizer.
others.title: Other players
others.description: Captions of what other players say (the game's sound on this PC), translated into your language if you like. They stay separate from your own captions: never in the chatbox, text to speech or history.
others.status_fallback_capture_failed: Couldn't capture {{program}}, so the default output is captured for now. Sigil tries the program again shortly.
others.log_capture_failed: Couldn't capture {{program}} ({{error}}). Capturing the default output instead; trying the program again in {{seconds}} s.

overlay.sources_none: Pick at least one source, or nothing is shown.
overlay.field_interim: Show text while it is still being recognized
overlay.field_clear_after_desc: Each line disappears this long after it last changed. 0 keeps lines until newer ones push them out.
overlay.test_caption: Sigil test caption · こんにちは · 안녕하세요 · مرحبا
overlay.window_desc: A small window that floats above your game and shows your captions. Mouse clicks go through it.
overlay.window_error: The caption window could not open: {{error}}
overlay.window_click_through_desc: Turn this off to move the window (drag it) or resize it (drag its edges), then turn it back on.
overlay.window_unlocked_hint: Drag to move · drag the edges to resize · turn "Let clicks go through it" back on in Sigil when done
overlay.btn_reset_position: Move it back to the bottom of the screen
overlay.window_vr_tip: In VR you can also pin this window with XSOverlay or OVR Toolkit (it is listed as "Sigil captions").
overlay.vr_desc: Shows your captions inside SteamVR. Sigil never starts SteamVR: the overlay appears once SteamVR is running and goes away when it closes.
overlay.vr_requires: The SteamVR overlay needs the OpenVR runtime (about 1 MB):
overlay.vr_running_with_error: Running, but SteamVR reported a problem: {{error}}
overlay.vr_waiting_not_installed: SteamVR is not installed on this PC. Install it from Steam, or use the caption window instead.
overlay.vr_waiting_quit: SteamVR closed. The overlay comes back when SteamVR runs again.
overlay.vr_waiting_failed: Could not connect to SteamVR yet; trying again.
overlay.vr_unavailable: Install the OpenVR runtime below to use the SteamVR overlay.
overlay.vr_too_old: This SteamVR is too old for the caption overlay. Update SteamVR in Steam.
overlay.vr_attach_head: In front of you (follows your head)
overlay.vr_attach_hand_desc: Floats just above the controller. Until the controller is on, it shows in front of you.
overlay.btn_recenter: Place it in front of me
overlay.vr_fallback_tip: If the overlay does not work with your headset, pin the caption window in XSOverlay or OVR Toolkit instead.

readings.title: Readings (furigana, romaji, pinyin)
readings.description: Adds how Japanese and Chinese captions are read: hiragana and romaji for Japanese, pinyin for Chinese. The readings go out next to the captions for displays that show them, and the last one appears below. Works offline on this PC.
readings.sources_none: Pick at least one caption source.
readings.interim: Also read captions while they are spoken
readings.interim_desc: Off: only finished lines get readings, which uses less CPU.
readings.where_desc: Lines without a known language are read only when they contain kana (Japanese); Chinese needs the caption's language. Pinyin shows tones as spoken, for example yí dìng and bú shì.
readings.desktop_only: Readings work in the desktop app.
readings.music_gate_desc: The local speech recognizer skips stretches that sound like music or singing. Speech over background music is kept.

onboarding.welcome_body: Live captions for your VRChat streams, with translation and voices when you want them. A few quick steps; everything can be changed later.
onboarding.audio_body: Sigil listens to this microphone and speaks through these speakers. You can change them later in Settings → Audio.
onboarding.stt_body: Sigil recognizes your speech on this PC. Models download once, after you agree.
onboarding.stt_other: Online engines and others are in the Speech to Text engine list.
onboarding.send_body: Pick one to set it up now, or finish and do it later under Integrations.
onboarding.done_body: Press Start in the bottom bar and speak. Translation, Text to Speech and Voice Changer are under Speech in the left menu.
onboarding.stt_autostart_hint: Captions start by themselves each time you open Sigil. Press Start once first to download the speech models.
